messages:
Jamie L: Ran a targeted perf sweep on master after the kernel-selector change. Seeing a 12-18% p99 step latency increase on 8xA100 PP 1F1B runs. Pretty consistent across seeds.
Ravi K: ugh. which part regressed — allreduce, wait stalls, or kvcache miss rate?
Jamie L: Allreduce time is slightly up (~6%), but comm/compute overlap dropped a lot. KV cache miss rate jumped from 2.1% to 9.4% on long sequences (2k). Attached a tiny log excerpt below.
Jamie L: ```
step 512: comm_ms=42 compute_ms=78 kv_miss=9.4%
step 513: comm_ms=45 compute_ms=80 kv_miss=9.1%
old master: comm_ms=39 compute_ms=83 kv_miss=2.3%
```
Sophia M: Interesting — kernel selector changed per-layer kernel for attention (switched to fused-attn v2) and we also bumped microbatcher heuristics to prefer smaller microbatches to reduce memory. Could be a batch packing interaction that increases KV churn.
Maria T: We saw something similar in canary last month when we enabled aggressive prefetch. Might be prefetch ordering interacting with 1F1B windowing.
Ravi K: Hypothesis: smaller microbatches -> more frequent kv cache evictions + more interleaving of allreduce windows -> worse overlap. Try increasing microbatch to 4->8 for that config and enable windowed_comm_prefetch=false to isolate.
Jamie L: Will run A/B: (A) revert to old kernel selector + microbatch=4, (B) keep new kernel + microbatch=8, (C) keep new kernel + microbatch=4 + prefetch=false. Hoping to tease apart.
perf-bot: run queued: perf-suite/pp-8xA100/longseq-sweep (id: ps-7821)
Sophia M: Also instrument a flamegraph for comm wait on every rank, and dump KV cache occupancy per layer. If occupancy oscillates with high variance that's a smoking gun.
Ravi K: If it's KV eviction thrash we could try a quick mitigation: increase per-layer kv_shard_prefetch_window from 32->128 steps for the experiment; that increases memory but might stabilize hits.
Maria T: I can spin up a dedicated test fleet with the memory headroom (add 50GB to each host). Schedule in ~30m.
Jamie L: Results from first A/B: (A) p99 back to baseline, (B) p99 improved over regressed but still +6% vs baseline, (C) p99 worst. KV miss in (A)=2.4%, (B)=6.2%, (C)=11.0%.
Jamie L: So kernel selector change alone isn't the root, it's the combination with microbatching heuristics + prefetch ordering.
Sophia M: Actionable: revert the kernel-selector toggle for 1F1B pipeline by default, add a runtime gate so we only use fused-attn v2 when microbatch >=8 and kv_prefetch_mode==windowed. Also add a transient kv_cache_profiler that records ttl/eviction stats during warmup.
Ravi K: I can prototype the gate in ~2hrs. We should also add a perf test that runs the microbatch sweep matrix so this doesn't regress silently.
Maria T: I'll hold off on fleet-wide kernel rollout and mark the PR with perf-needed.
Jamie L: Thanks. Final note: while debugging I found a small bug in the microbatcher where leftover padding was being considered in batch packing score — created a tiny fix and attached patch link: https://internal/repo/patch/pp-microbat-pack-fix
Sophia M: Nice catch. Let's get the gate + profiler + microbatch test in first, then re-run the kernel rollout with staging A/B.
Ravi K: Agreed. I'll post the experiment commands here once the gate is up.
Jamie L: TL;DR: regression is an emergent property of kernel selection + microbatch heuristics + prefetch ordering. Short-term: add gate and profiler. Mid-term: tighter microbatch packing invariants and a perf-matrix test. :thumbsup:
